To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) happy faces with visible teeth were rated as less intense and less prototypical than the same faces when teeth were covered; (2) participants spent less time looking at the mouth region of faces with covered teeth; (3) the mouth region was the most informative region for happy faces with visible and covered teeth.
(1) teeth visibility in smiling faces can influence emotionality ratings; and (2) teeth visibility in happy faces can influence the initial attention of observers.
